newsitem.title: USA: Calif. agriculture damages estimated at $155 mln.
newsitem.headline: Calif. agriculture damages estimated at $155 mln.

text.p: California officials estimated on Friday initial flood damage to California agriculture at nearly $155 million.
California's Department of Food and Agriculture said damage to infrastructure, private levees, farm equipment, buildings and irrigation systems came to $68.3 million.
The department said 25,000 acres of crops have been lost, with an additional 92,500 acres damaged by the rain and flooding, at an estimated loss of about $51 million.
Officials said these estimates were preliminary and were likely to change as more areas are surveyed.

Livestock and dairy losses, including losses in milk production, dead animals and destroyed feed, were estimated at about $22.4 million, the department said. Milk production losses alone were estimated at $9.9 million.

The commodities most impacted were winegrapes, alfalfa, wheat and broccoli, the department said. Winegrape losses were estimated at $11.7 million, alfalfa at $8.5 million, wheat and barley at $4.6 million and broccoli at $3.2 million.
The department said walnut losses were estimated at $2.9 million, while plum and prune losses were put at $1.9 million and almond losses at $1.5 million.

State Agriculture Secretary Ann Veneman, who toured flood damaged areas with Governor Pete Wilson on Friday, said several counties were having trouble assessing damages because floodwaters have not subsided in many agricultural areas.

"It will be some time before we know the overall impact of these floods because many crops are currently dormant," she said. "However, damage to infrastructure, buildings, farm equipment, land and irrigation systems are of great concern to growers in the long term."
